::::: {#chapter-1 .chapter}
## Do light and fire synergistically control stand density?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](photos/chapter1.jpg){fig-alt="Researcher is kneeling and measuring the stem diameter of a bolting longleaf pine tree"}
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
This chapter of my dissertation is on-going, with a four-year field study that aims to determine:

- How light availability relates to growth of bolting longleaf pines
- How size relates to survival of bolting longleaf pines

:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#chapter-2 .chapter}
## How do pyrophytic oaks impact fuel bed flammability?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](photos/chapter2.jpg){fig-alt="Longleaf pine savanna at golden hour, with the understory of grasses and forbs glowing golden in the setting sun"}
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
The field work for this chapter of my dissertation will begin very soon! I will be taking field measurements and conducting experimental burns to quantify:

- How pyrophytic oak density relates to the fuel load and the relative abundance of different fuel types in the understory
- How the fuel load and relative abundance of different fuels shape fuel bed flammability and fire behavior
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#chapter-3 .chapter}
## How do pyrophytic oaks impact the understory plant community?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](photos/chapter3.jpg){fig-alt="Longleaf pine landscape with a considerable number of hardwoods in the understory"}
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
I'm currently analyzing Carolina Vegetation Survey data, and hope to conduct a follow-up field study in Summer 2027, to investigate:

- How pyrophytic oaks in the canopy influence community composition in the understory
- How pyrophytic oaks in stunted, fire-shrub growth forms might influence community composition differently 
:::
::::
:::::
